channel.title: AI Security Paper Digest
channel.description: Curated papers on AI security from ArXiv and ACL

item.title: One Pic is All it Takes: Poisoning Visual Document Retrieval Augmented Generation with a Single Image
item.description:
Summary

  • Shows that visual document RAG (VD-RAG) is vulnerable to poisoning attacks via a single adversarial image injected into the KB.
  • Demonstrates targeted poisoning to spread disinformation for specific queries/groups of queries.
  • Demonstrates a universal poisoning objective that can force denial-of-service for any user query.
  • Evaluates attacks in white-box and black-box settings across multiple datasets, retrievers, and vision-language generators.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Ezzeldin Shereen', 'Dan Ristea', 'Shae McFadden', 'Burak Hasircioglu', 'Vasilios Mavroudis', 'Chris Hicks']
  • Tags: ['AI security', 'RAG/VD-RAG poisoning', 'Adversarial examples', 'Attack evaluation']

item.title: Towards Physically Realizable Adversarial Attenuation Patch against SAR Object Detection
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes an Adversarial Attenuation Patch (AAP) to degrade SAR (Synthetic Aperture Radar) object detection.
  • Targets physical realizability by modeling/aligning the attack with signal-level electronic jamming and energy constraints.
  • Demonstrates reduced detection performance with high stealth/imperceptibility and reports transferability across different detection models.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Yiming Zhang', 'Weibo Qin', 'Feng Wang']
  • Tags: ['Adversarial Attacks', 'Physical-layer/Physical-world Attacks', 'SAR Target Detection']

item.title: When Surfaces Lie: Exploiting Wrinkle-Induced Attention Shift to Attack Vision-Language Models
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes a physically plausible, non-rigid “wrinkle-induced” visual perturbation method for vision-language models (VLMs).
  • Uses a parametric, structural deformation approach inspired by 3D fabric mechanics, generating photorealistic wrinkle fields and surface-consistent appearance changes.
  • Employs optimization-based search with a hierarchical fitness function to balance naturalness and adversarial effectiveness.
  • Evaluates transferability by optimizing on a zero-shot classification proxy task and testing on generative VLM tasks (image captioning and visual QA), showing consistent performance degradation across SOTA VLMs.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Chengyin Hu', 'Xuemeng Sun', 'Jiajun Han', 'Qike Zhang', 'Xiang Chen', 'Xin Wang', 'Yiwei Wei', 'Jiahua Long']
  • Tags: ['adversarial examples', 'physical/robustness attacks', 'vision-language models', 'optimization-based attack']

item.title: PPEDCRF: Privacy-Preserving Enhanced Dynamic CRF for Location-Privacy Protection for Sequence Videos with Minimal Detection Degradation
item.description:
Summary

  • Studies location-privacy leakage from dashcam sequence videos using a background-based retrieval attacker that matches visual cues to street-view imagery.
  • Proposes PPEDCRF, a privacy-preserving framework that injects calibrated perturbations into inferred location-sensitive background regions.
  • Uses a dynamic CRF for temporal consistency/region tracking, a hierarchical sensitivity model to allocate perturbation strength, and a utility-preserving noise injection module to limit degradation to detection/segmentation.
  • Reports improved privacy (reduced retrieval accuracy/top-k success) while maintaining competitive detection/segmentation utility versus several anonymization/noise baselines.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Bo Ma', 'Jinsong Wu', 'Weiqi Yan', 'Catherine Shi', 'Minh Nguyen']
  • Tags: ['privacy attacks', 'location inference', 'video anonymization', 'adversarial/perturbation-based defense', 'conditional random fields']

item.title: Seeing Through the Chain: Mitigate Hallucination in Multimodal Reasoning Models via CoT Compression and Contrastive Preference Optimization
item.description:
Summary

  • Analyzes why multimodal reasoning models hallucinate, attributing it to increased language-prior reliance and insufficient use of visual cues during reasoning traces.
  • Proposes C3PO: Chain-of-Thought compression to filter redundant reasoning tokens while preserving task-relevant information from multimodal inputs.
  • Introduces contrastive preference optimization using reasoning-enhanced preference tuning with high-quality AI feedback to correct low-quality reasoning traces.
  • Uses a “hallucination-inducing mechanism” with crafted inducers to generate informative negative signals for contrastive learning and reduces hallucinations across multiple models/benchmarks.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Hao Fang', 'Jinyu Li', 'Jiawei Kong', 'Tianqu Zhuang', 'Kuofeng Gao', 'Bin Chen', 'Shu-Tao Xia']
  • Tags: ['hallucination-mitigation', 'multimodal-reasoning', 'contrastive-preference-optimization', 'chain-of-thought-compression']

item.title: Understanding the Risks of Asphalt Art to the Reliability of Vision-Based Perception Systems
item.description:
Summary

  • Studies how asphalt art (including adversarially crafted patterns) affects vision-based pedestrian detection reliability.
  • Evaluates object detection performance on composited crosswalk scenes under benign vs adversarial conditions.
  • Demonstrates that certain visual patterns can both obscure real pedestrians and induce false detections, indicating a vulnerability in surveillance perception models.
  • Argues for robustness to environmental visual variations when designing pedestrian detection systems.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Jin Ma', 'Abyad Enan', 'Long Cheng', 'Mashrur Chowdhury']
  • Tags: ['adversarial examples', 'computer vision security', 'object detection robustness', 'surveillance vulnerability']

item.title: Why Instruction-Based Unlearning Fails in Diffusion Models?
item.description:
Summary

  • Studies inference-time instruction-based unlearning in diffusion (image) generation models.
  • Finds that natural-language unlearning instructions systematically fail to suppress targeted concepts across concepts and prompt variants.
  • Analyzes internal mechanisms (CLIP text encoder and cross-attention during denoising) showing attention reductions are not sustained, so concept representations persist.
  • Concludes effective unlearning likely requires interventions beyond prompt-level language control.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Zeliang Zhang', 'Rui Sun', 'Jiani Liu', 'Qi Wu', 'Chenliang Xu']
  • Tags: ['model unlearning', 'diffusion models', 'prompt/instruction-based control', 'concept suppression', 'cross-attention analysis']

item.title: Modular Energy Steering for Safe Text-to-Image Generation with Foundation Models
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes a training-free, inference-time “energy steering” framework for text-to-image diffusion/flow-matching models using gradient feedback from frozen vision-language foundation models.
  • Aims to improve safety behavior without fine-tuning or curated datasets by applying energy-based sampling/latent feedback at each generation step.
  • Reports robustness against NSFW red-teaming benchmarks and supports multi-target steering while maintaining quality for benign prompts.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Yaoteng Tan', 'Zikui Cai', 'M. Salman Asif']
  • Tags: ['AI safety', 'Text-to-Image', 'Attack/Red-teaming robustness', 'Inference-time defenses', 'Energy-based steering']

item.title: Low-Effort Jailbreak Attacks Against Text-to-Image Safety Filters
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes and studies low-effort, prompt-only jailbreak strategies that bypass safety filters in text-to-image generative systems without model access or optimization.
  • Introduces a taxonomy of visual jailbreak techniques (e.g., artistic reframing, material substitution, lifestyle aesthetic camouflage, ambiguous action substitution).
  • Evaluates attacks across multiple state-of-the-art text-to-image models and reports high attack success rates (up to 74.47%).

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Ahmed B Mustafa', 'Zihan Ye', 'Yang Lu', 'Michael P Pound', 'Shreyank N Gowda']
  • Tags: ['jailbreaking', 'prompt injection/safety bypass', 'text-to-image security', 'adversarial prompting']

item.title: SafeRoPE: Risk-specific Head-wise Embedding Rotation for Safe Generation in Rectified Flow Transformers
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes SafeRoPE, a lightweight safety method for transformer-based text-to-image diffusion (MMDiT) using head-wise rotary positional embedding (RoPE) perturbations.
  • Identifies safety-critical attention heads and unsafe feature subspaces, computing a Latent Risk Score (LRS) by projecting embeddings onto these subspaces.
  • Uses risk-specific, head-wise RoPE rotation on query/key embeddings to suppress unsafe semantics while preserving benign image quality.
  • Claims state-of-the-art trade-offs between harmful content mitigation and utility preservation.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Xiang Yang', 'Feifei Li', 'Mi Zhang', 'Geng Hong', 'Xiaoyu You', 'Min Yang']
  • Tags: ['AI safety', 'text-to-image diffusion', 'prompt/semantic safety mitigation', 'attention-head subspaces', 'RoPE perturbation']

item.title: Moir\'e Video Authentication: A Physical Signature Against AI Video Generation
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes a physics-based authentication method for distinguishing real camera videos from AI-generated videos using Moiré effect signatures.
  • Derives a Moiré motion invariant relating fringe phase and grating displacement, largely independent of distance and specific grating structure.
  • Verifier extracts two optical signals from video and checks their correlation to classify authenticity.
  • Validated on real-captured and multi-generator AI videos, showing different correlation signatures between real and generated content.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Yuan Qing', 'Kunyu Zheng', 'Lingxiao Li', 'Boqing Gong', 'Chang Xiao']
  • Tags: ['video-authentication', 'physical-signatures', 'AI-generated-content-detection', 'Moiré-effect']

item.title: Tex3D: Objects as Attack Surfaces via Adversarial 3D Textures for Vision-Language-Action Models
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes Tex3D, a framework to optimize physically realizable adversarial 3D textures targeting vision-language-action (VLA) robotic manipulation models.
  • Introduces Foreground-Background Decoupling (FBD) to enable differentiable end-to-end texture optimization through the VLA objective.
  • Develops Trajectory-Aware Adversarial Optimization (TAAO) to maintain attack effectiveness across long-horizon behaviors and diverse physical viewpoints.
  • Shows large performance degradation and high task failure rates (up to 96.7%) in simulation and real-robot experiments.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Jiawei Chen', 'Simin Huang', 'Jiawei Du', 'Shuaihang Chen', 'Yu Tian', 'Mingjie Wei', 'Chao Yu', 'Zhaoxia Yin']
  • Tags: ['adversarial attacks', '3D adversarial textures', 'vision-language-action (VLA)', 'physical-world robustness']

item.title: Optimus: A Robust Defense Framework for Mitigating Toxicity while Fine-Tuning Conversational AI
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes Optimus, a defense framework to mitigate toxicity introduced during fine-tuning on untrusted datasets.
  • Uses a training-free toxicity classification scheme that repurposes safety alignment from commodity LLMs to reduce reliance on imperfect/biased toxicity detectors.
  • Employs dual alignment (synthetic “healing data” plus Direct Preference Optimization) to steer models toward safer behavior.
  • Reports robustness against adaptive adversarial and jailbreak attacks and improved performance over prior defenses (e.g., StarDSS).

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Aravind Cheruvu', 'Shravya Kanchi', 'Sifat Muhammad Abdullah', 'Nicholas Kong', 'Daphne Yao', 'Murtuza Jadliwala', 'Bimal Viswanath']
  • Tags: ['LLM safety', 'Toxicity mitigation', 'Defense against jailbreaks', 'Robustness to classifier bias']

item.title: Towards Distillation-Resistant Large Language Models: An Information-Theoretic Perspective
item.description:
Summary

  • Studies model extraction (distillation) attacks against black-box LLMs, including logit-based distillation.
  • Proposes an information-theoretic defense by minimizing conditional mutual information (CMI) related to teacher logits and queries.
  • Introduces a learned transformation that “purifies” outputs to remove distillation-relevant information while maintaining task utility.
  • Evaluates across multiple LLMs and distillation algorithms, showing reduced distillation performance with preserved accuracy.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Hao Fang', 'Tianyi Zhang', 'Tianqu Zhuang', 'Jiawei Kong', 'Kuofeng Gao', 'Bin Chen', 'Leqi Liang', 'Shu-Tao Xia', 'Ke Xu']
  • Tags: ['Model Extraction', 'Distillation Resistance', 'Logit-based Attacks', 'Information-Theoretic Defenses']

item.title: RuleForge: Automated Generation and Validation for Web Vulnerability Detection at Scale
item.description:
Summary

  • Presents RuleForge, an automated system that generates JSON-based HTTP detection rules for CVE exploits from structured Nuclei templates.
  • Introduces an LLM-as-a-judge confidence validation mechanism to balance sensitivity vs. specificity and reduce false positives versus synthetic-only testing.
  • Uses a parallel candidate generation and iterative refinement strategy with continuous feedback loops for improved rule quality.
  • Discusses extensions for generating rules from unstructured sources and a proof-of-concept agentic workflow for multi-event-type detection.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Ayush Garg', 'Sophia Hager', 'Jacob Montiel', 'Aditya Tiwari', 'Michael Gentile', 'Zach Reavis', 'David Magnotti', 'Wayne Fullen']
  • Tags: ['Web Application Security', 'Vulnerability Detection', 'Automated Rule Generation', 'LLM-as-a-Judge', 'HTTP Signatures']

item.title: OSCAR: Orchestrated Self-verification and Cross-path Refinement
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes an inference-time hallucination mitigation method for diffusion language models (DLMs) using their denoising trajectories as an uncertainty signal.
  • Introduces commitment uncertainty localization by flagging token positions with high cross-chain entropy before incorrect self-consistent commitments propagate.
  • Presents trajectory-level assessment metrics (e.g., cross-chain divergence-at-hallucination) to compare localization methods.
  • Introduces OSCAR: runs parallel denoising chains with randomized reveal orders, detects high-uncertainty positions, then performs targeted remasking conditioned on retrieved evidence.
  • Experiments on multiple QA benchmarks show reduced hallucinations and improved factual accuracy versus uncertainty detectors trained externally.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Yash Shah', 'Abhijit Chakraborty', 'Naresh Kumar Devulapally', 'Vishnu Lokhande', 'Vivek Gupta']
  • Tags: ['hallucination-mitigation', 'uncertainty-guided-generation', 'diffusion-language-models', 'inference-time-defense']

item.title: When Reward Hacking Rebounds: Understanding and Mitigating It with Representation-Level Signals
item.description:
Summary

  • Studies reward hacking in RL for LLMs, focusing on how models exploit shortcuts to pass coding evaluations without solving the intended task.
  • Uses an environment-manipulation testbed where models can rewrite evaluator code, enabling controlled analysis of hacking and a reproducible three-phase “rebound” pattern.
  • Identifies representation-level directions (shortcut, deception, evaluation awareness) that correlate with hacking behavior and can serve as detection proxies.
  • Proposes Advantage Modification, a training-time defense that incorporates shortcut concept scores into GRPO advantage computation to penalize hacking rollouts.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Rui Wu', 'Ruixiang Tang']
  • Tags: ['reward hacking', 'reinforcement learning', 'representation-level detection', 'training-time defenses']

item.title: No Attacker Needed: Unintentional Cross-User Contamination in Shared-State LLM Agents
item.description:
Summary

  • Studies unintentional cross-user contamination (UCC) in shared-state LLM agents where persisted task state/knowledge is reused across different user identities.
  • Formalizes and evaluates UCC via a controlled protocol, proposes a taxonomy of contamination types, and measures contamination rates across two shared-state mechanisms.
  • Finds that benign interactions (no attacker) can silently cause wrong answers due to scope-mismatched artifacts, and that write-time sanitization is only partially effective—especially when shared state includes executable artifacts.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Tiankai Yang', 'Jiate Li', 'Yi Nian', 'Shen Dong', 'Ruiyao Xu', 'Ryan Rossi', 'Kaize Ding', 'Yue Zhao']
  • Tags: ['privacy/security risk', 'cross-user contamination', 'shared-state/agent memory', 'input/output sanitization']
